problem: Semantic maps for ObjectNav are built from single-frame segmentation with heuristic projection, so noisy predictions (especially far objects) create false goals and are not integrated with the planners; Habitat Challenge success stayed below ~60%.
motivation: Semantic map quality drives ObjectNav success and path efficiency. An embodied agent can refine perception by fusing several frames from its own motion, and combining RL skills with classic map-based planning can be more robust than either alone.
key_idea: Build a two-level interactive semantic map: SegmATRon refines per-frame segmentation at inference through a learned fusion loss over a backward or forward frame buffer, followed by erosion/dilation/accumulation/fading filtering into a BEV map, all used inside SkillTron, which switches between PONI/A* map-based skills and RL skills.
insight: Multi-frame test-time adaptation of the segmenter improves the accumulated map and navigation, but only a moderate number of extra frames helps: 2 extra frames is best for navigation (SR 0.59), while 4 gives 0.57 and slows the pipeline. Backward sequences give the best map quality (Closeness-sigmoid 0.175, IoU 0.446 at 4 steps) versus forward. Filtering hyperparameters (alpha=0.9, T=2) matter for false positives. A 15° turn angle is worse than 30° (SR 0.49-0.51 vs 0.57-0.59).
method: SegmATRon interactive segmentation: OneFormer (Swin-L) segmenter plus a DETR-decoder fusion module that predicts a learned fusion loss over the frame sequence; OneFormer weights are updated by gradient step at inference, then re-predicts the first frame.
Frame buffer order: backward (B) uses {I_t..I_{t-n}}; forward (F) uses future frames {I_t..I_{t+n}}, so map updates are delayed. Buffers of 2, 3 or 5 images (1, 2 or 4 extra frames).

Semantic map filtering: local map from depth+pose+mask; erosion then dilation; global map fused by accumulation (+1 on goal cells) and fading (multiply by alpha<1 on uncovered goal cells); goal cell if value > T.
Map-based skills: PONI potential-function exploration (area+object potentials, UNet) on a 16-class multilayer map; A* path planning to the nearest goal cell once mapped; stop threshold 0.84.
Learning-based skills: DDPPO-trained exploration (trained jointly with PointNav and flee, frozen CLIP encoder) and Goal Reacher with a 'not sure' action for false positives (SkillFusion).

Skill Fusion Decider: in exploration, use RL when critic score exceeds tau, otherwise PONI; upon seeing the goal use the RL goal reacher, switching to map-based planner once the goal is mapped; revert to exploration if the goal vanishes from the map or view.
Training of segmenter: fine-tuned from ADE20k weights on offline HM3DSem v0.2 sequences (1160 train points, 144 val points), mapping 1624 categories to 150 ADE20k classes.

setting.backbone: OneFormer Swin-L + DETR fusion decoder (SegmATRon, fine-tuned); PONI UNet; DDPPO RL policies with frozen CLIP encoder
setting.training_data: Segmenter fine-tuned from ADE20k weights on custom HM3DSem v0.2 image sequences (1160 train points, 144 val points, sequences of 4 actions); RL skills and PONI trained per SkillFusion/PONI
setting.action_space: discrete: stop, forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30° (15° in ablation); look up/down in the Habitat challenge setting
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT semantics used only for evaluating map quality)

numbers_note: Values are printed as fractions (0.59), not percentages. Evaluation uses a custom 108-episode subset of HM3DSem v0.2 validation; the ICanFly and Host_74441_Team baselines come from the Habitat Challenge 2023 test-standard leaderboard, so they are not directly comparable.
results: SkillTron with SegmATRon (B, 2 steps) reaches SR 0.59 / SPL 0.28 / SoftSPL 0.36, beating the SkillFusion challenge winner (0.55/0.26/0.34) and the single-frame fine-tuned OneFormer variant (0.57/0.28/0.35). Interactive segmentation gives +2% success over single frame.
limitations: Segmentation network is resource-demanding; inference-time adaptation slows the pipeline (time limit raised to 1500 s per episode).
Evaluated only in simulation on a small 108-episode custom subset, with gains of only 1-2 points.
